name: dac7
what_it_holds: Python tooling (138 commits) to build and validate DAC7 declarations for French tax authority (DGFiP): revised XSD schema, JSON schemas for platform-operator/entity-seller/individual-seller flat files, example files adapted from official DGFiP specs, CLI to build/validate/encrypt declarations. No actual DAC7 statistics or aggregate reported-income data -- only the filing schema/tooling. License: Etalab-2.0 (schemas/examples).
why_useful: Marginal: confirms the DAC7 declaration format and required host/seller fields; no actual Airbnb or STR data.
themes: Airbnb host-side datasets: superhost/multi-listing/professional host panels, host earnings, DAC7 platform-reporting statistics, IRS/tax authority STR income stats
why_all: Marginal: confirms the DAC7 declaration format and required host/seller fields; no actual Airbnb or STR data.

Gives the exact data schema platforms like Airbnb must report to EU tax authorities under DAC7 (seller income, number of transactions, property addresses) -- useful for understanding what a DAC7 aggregate-statistics release would even look like if one is ever published, and for identifying the right EU government portals to check for aggregate DAC7 statistics.

name: dac7-dpi-client-php
what_it_holds: PHP client for the Polish DAC7 DPI API, letting a platform operator submit seller/host reports (DPI-FR registration, DPI-IS seller reports) to the Polish tax administration (KAS).
why_useful: Points to a specific national API (Poland) where, in principle, aggregate/statistical releases about DAC7-reported platform income could originate; no data itself.
themes: Airbnb host-side datasets: superhost/multi-listing/professional host panels, host earnings, DAC7 platform-reporting statistics, IRS/tax authority STR income stats
why_all: Points to a specific national API (Poland) where, in principle, aggregate/statistical releases about DAC7-reported platform income could originate; no data itself.

name: bcgov/House-Policy-STRDSS
what_it_holds: British Columbia government's 'Short Term Rental Data Sharing System' -- full-stack app (backend, frontend, PostgreSQL) that platforms operating in BC (Airbnb included) are required to report host/listing data into under BC's Short-Term Rental Accommodations Act. 2,764 commits, Apache-2.0 license. The repo itself is the government's internal software, not a public dataset or API; no public statistics endpoint found in the fetched README (only CI/CD/release docs).
why_useful: Confirms a real, government-mandated, DAC7-style platform-reporting regime exists for STR data in BC/Canada; worth a human checking gov.bc.ca or BC's open-data portal directly for any published aggregate statistics derived from this system (would be genuinely point-in-time regulatory data on host counts/compliance), even though the GitHub repo itself has no data.
themes: Airbnb host-side datasets: superhost/multi-listing/professional host panels, host earnings, DAC7 platform-reporting statistics, IRS/tax authority STR income stats
why_all: Confirms a real, government-mandated, DAC7-style platform-reporting regime exists for STR data in BC/Canada; worth a human checking gov.bc.ca or BC's open-data portal directly for any published aggregate statistics derived from this system (would be genuinely point-in-time regulatory data on host counts/compliance), even though the GitHub repo itself has no data.

name: 2892480843/CityPulse
what_it_holds: AI agent for predicting emerging/trending destination cities for Qunar (Ctrip-owned Chinese OTA) with a scoring/backtest architecture. Data files (city_score_snapshot.csv, daily_signal_sample.csv, signals_demo_panel.csv: 13 cities x 45 days x 9 indicators = 5,031 rows, feature_dictionary.csv, reference_sources.csv) are explicitly labeled SYNTHETIC/demo, not real Qunar order data. MIT license, 32 commits.
why_useful: The METHOD (a documented multi-signal, time-cutoff-validated nowcasting architecture for city-level Chinese travel demand) could be a template even though the data itself is fake; not a data source.
themes: Agoda, Trip.com, Tujia, Xiaozhu, Meituan, MakeMyTrip, OYO, Traveloka datasets and scrapers (APAC OTA and STR platforms)
why_all: The METHOD (a documented multi-signal, time-cutoff-validated nowcasting architecture for city-level Chinese travel demand) could be a template even though the data itself is fake; not a data source.

name: chuqinyao/citypulse-ai-qunar-2026
what_it_holds: Competition entry (2026) using time-series signals to forecast trending Qunar destinations; data is explicitly is_synthetic=true, 12 cities x 180 days = 2,160 rows, no real Qunar order data. MIT license, 7 commits.
why_useful: Same caveat as CityPulse above — a nowcasting-method reference only, not usable as a data source; documents rolling 7/14/28-day feature construction that could inspire a MIDAS-style APAC demand nowcast (gap #17).
